subject: Brightline MSA: term, notice windows, and termination-for-convenience - proposed compromise
messages:
From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@brightline.io>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightline Legal <legal@brightline.io>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brightline MSA - Term/Auto‑Renew Redlines

Hi Chloe,

Attached is Brightline's redline of the MSA (see Brightline_MSA_redline_v2.docx). High-level comments:

- Auto‑renew: we can accept a 1x automatic renewal but need a 60‑90 day notice window before renewal for enterprise deals; shorter pilots should be allowed a 30‑60 day window.
- Termination for convenience: our legal team is pushing for unilateral termination-for-convenience with 30 days' notice and pro‑rated refund. We understand this is atypical for vendors; open to negotiation.
- Sunset / offboarding: we require a guaranteed data handback process and a defined escrow for customer data.

Can you confirm Redwood's positions on the three items above? If you prefer, we can schedule a 30‑minute call.

Thanks,

Sarah Miller
Head of Partnerships, Brightline Health
sarah.miller@brightline.io
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: Brightline_MSA_redline_v2.docx (MS Word redline)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@brightline.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline MSA - Term/Auto‑Renew Redlines

Hi Sarah — thanks for the redline and the clear calls. Quick read-through and our initial position below; Karthik/Ben, looping you in for pricing/contract impact.

1) Auto‑renew / notice windows:
- We can support a staggered notice approach but need objective thresholds:
  * Monthly/pilot agreements (TCV < $25k / month): 30 days notice.
  * Annual SaaS commercial agreements: 60 days notice.
  * Enterprise multi‑year commitments: 90 days notice.
- Notice should be counted from renewal effective date and should be communicated in writing.

2) Termination for convenience:
- Redwood does not typically accept unilateral 30‑day one‑way termination for convenience for enterprise deals due to operational and capacity planning impact.
- Proposed compromise: mutual termination for convenience (either party) with 90 days' notice OR one‑way termination for convenience by the customer only where the customer pays an offboarding fee equal to 3 months' average committed spend and Redwood provides 90 days of transition support.
- An alternative fallback we can consider: a 120‑day notice (customer one‑way) with no fee but pro‑rated credits for unused prepaid amounts.

3) Sunset / offboarding 
- We will commit to a documented handback process and delivery of customer data exports within 30 days of effective termination, plus a short-term transition SLA. For regulated customers we can add an escrow or KMS handoff addendum; will need security sign‑off.

I attached a proposed redline (proposed_redline_msa_chloe_v3.docx) that captures the above. If any of these are deal blockers, flag them and we can schedule a call.

Best,

Chloe Martin
Principal, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_redline_msa_chloe_v3.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Brightline MSA - Term/Auto‑Renew Redlines (revenue impact)

Chloe — quick internal take, copied Laura for finance:

- I support the staggered notice windows; they line up with how we price and handoff pilots vs enterprise.
- Termination-for-convenience: strong preference for either mutual TOC or customer one‑way with offboarding fee. One‑way 30 days is a no-go for us.
- If we accept 60 days across the board it materially increases churn risk and operational costs; attached is a rough tearsheet on revenue impact (Tearsheet_revenue_impact.xlsx).

My recommended negotiation posture: hold firm on 90 days for enterprise, 60 for annual commercial, 30 for pilots; accept the offboarding-fee compromise as written under Chloes's draft. If they insist on 30‑day unilateral, push for a service credit cap and data escrow terms.

Ben
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline MSA - Term/Auto‑Renew Redlines

Hi Sarah — appreciate the patience while we reviewed. Attached are two artifacts: a cleaned redline (proposed_redline_msa_chloe_v3.docx) and a short summary of changes (summary_of_changes.pdf). High‑level note of the changes we made so you can brief your legal team quickly:

- Introduced staggered notice windows (30/60/90 days) tied to explicit thresholds so both sides have certainty.
- Replaced customer's proposed unilateral 30‑day termination‑for‑convenience with a compromise: mutual TOC with 90 days' notice OR customer one‑way TOC with an offboarding fee equal to 3 months' committed spend + 90 days of transition support.
- Added a 'sunset escape' mechanism: if active usage drops below 10% of baseline for 90 consecutive days, either party may initiate a termination path with 60 days' notice and prioritized offboarding support. This is intended for long‑tail product sunsetting scenarios.
- Clarified data handback SLAs and optional escrow/KMS addendum for regulated customers.

If any of the above are firm no‑gos for Brightline, let me know which specific line items so we can consider targeted concessions (e.g., extend notice to 120 days in lieu of offboarding fee). Otherwise, would you be available for a 30‑minute call Mon/Tue next week to finalize?

Best,

Chloe Martin
Principal, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_redline_msa_chloe_v3.docx; summary_of_changes.pdf

Chloe — thanks for the clear summary and for putting numbers on the table. A few quick points from Brightline legal:

- The staggered notice language is promising; legal will validate thresholds but this is easier to work with than a single blanket term.
- The 'sunset escape' clause is new — we like the intent but need the baseline usage definition spelled out (how baseline is calculated, what counts as 'active usage').
- Termination for convenience: we'll escalate your offboarding‑fee compromise internally. If Redwood can accept a 60‑day one‑way option for pilots (TCV < $25k) we may be able to accept 90 days for enterprise.

Let's do a 30‑minute sync Monday, Aug 23 at 10am PT to go line‑by-line. I'll ask legal to provide a short counter for the TOC paragraph before then.

Appreciate the flexibility — Sarah

Sarah Miller
Head of Partnerships, Brightline Health
